She had poorly localized discomfort in the left diaphragmatic region on deep inspiration and loose stools over the preceding three days. Three days before presentation she had returned from a three-week trip to Western Australia, and 18 months earlier she had traveled to Vietnam. On examination she appeared well but was febrile at 38.0°C and tachypnoeic at 22 breaths/min, with all other observations normal. Examination of all other systems was unremarkable. Blood tests showed severe neutrophilia (18.9 × 10⁹/L; reference range 2.0-8.1), raised C reactive protein (354 mg/L; reference value <10), and normal renal and liver biochemistry. Chest radiography and urinalysis were normal. Blood cultures taken at presentation were negative.

She reported slow deterioration in vision from age 50, though she could still drive. Her mother was registered blind and had Parkinson's disease with dementia. On examination, she had a spastic gait with normal power in lower limbs but increased tone and sustained ankle clonus. Reflexes were brisk with flexor plantar responses. She had mild reduction in visual acuity and dyschromatopsia, but no detectable visual field defect and preserved pupillary light reflexes. CSF analysis showed presence of oligoclonal bands. His symptoms began with headache and abdominal pain, with an initial temperature of 38.6°C and pale skin. He experienced persistent upper abdominal pain and recurrent fevers. The patient reported nausea, occasional diarrhea, headache, myalgias, fatigue, and occasional dizziness. He described nearly constant periumbilical pain radiating to the left lower quadrant, with occasional blood in stools. His height was 132 cm (1st percentile), weight 26.8 kg (1st percentile), with recent 1 kg weight loss. Physical examination revealed pale skin and mucosa, distended abdomen with mild tenderness in right upper and left lower quadrants, and ecchymoses on the shins. He had visited the Dominican Republic 3 months prior. Laboratory tests showed severe microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 6.7 g/dL), elevated inflammatory markers (ESR >140 mm/hr, CRP 143.2 mg/liter), and elevated ferritin (320 μg/L).

He consumed cooked shrimp and lobster and a small amount of raw tuna. On the second-to-last day of the trip, he developed nausea, vomiting, and nonbloody diarrhea. He reported weakness, anorexia, decreased urine output with dark urine, and blurry vision during fever episodes. His medical history included degenerative knee disease with previous glucocorticoid injections. case:
23-year-old Korean female with 6 months of recurrent bilateral visual field defects and headache, worsening 1 month before presentation. She presented with 1 day of left-eye visual disturbance and visual field defect, then developed sudden left-sided hearing loss 2 days later. Three weeks later, she reported right-eye visual field defect, and 2 days after that was admitted for tinnitus, severe headache, and arm numbness. She denied diabetes, hypertension, connective tissue disease, tuberculosis, hematologic disease, cardiovascular disease, oral contraceptive use, and pregnancy. Initial exam showed reactive pupils without relative afferent pupillary defect, visual acuity 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye, normal intraocular pressure, and no anterior segment abnormalities. Laboratory testing and rheumatologic/hematologic workup were unremarkable except for mildly elevated CSF protein (74.4 mg/dL) without oligoclonal bands.

case:
A 73-year-old woman with a 10-year history of severe paraspinal muscle atrophy and cerebellar ataxia. Symptoms began at age 63 with slight stooping posture, then progressive gait instability requiring a walking stick by age 68 and difficulty climbing stairs by age 70. Exam showed moderate neck flexion weakness, mild proximal limb weakness, poor tandem gait balance without limb ataxia, and MMSE 25/30. Laboratory findings included elevated creatine kinase, normal blood and CSF lactate, slightly low TSH, elevated antithyroglobulin and antithyroid peroxidase antibodies, elevated rheumatoid factor, and mild ANA positivity. EMG showed mild myopathic changes. Audiometry revealed sensorineural high-frequency hearing loss, and Holter monitoring showed frequent premature contractions.

case:
A 2-year-old Korean male was admitted for evaluation and management of left hip pain. Physical examination revealed several palpable lymph nodes in the left inguinal area and an ill-defined heterogeneous mass-like lesion in the left anteromedial muscle. Peripheral blood examination showed hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, white blood cell count 6.83 × 10^9/L, platelet count 182 × 10^9/L, and 5 atypical lymphocytes per 100 white blood cells. Immunophenotyping of neoplastic cells showed positivity for CD45 (99.0%), CD19 (94.84%), CD10 (27.64%), CD20 (94.24%), HLA-DR (95.70%), surface IgG lambda (96.45%), CD13 (22.46%), and CD117 (22.22%), and negativity for CD34 (0.01%), Tdt (0.64%), myeloperoxidase (0.01%), and various T-cell and myeloid markers.

case:
44-year-old man with 1 month of intermittent, nonexertional substernal burning chest pain lasting hours to days, temporarily relieved by antacids/omeprazole, now presenting with severe pain radiating to the left arm that awoke him from sleep 1 hour earlier, associated with nausea and nonbloody vomiting. He denied dyspnea, edema, fever, cough, trauma, or prior thrombotic/bleeding/neurologic symptoms. Past history was unremarkable, but he recalled a platelet count around 600,000/mm³ noted 12 years earlier and reported intermittent pruritus after hot showers. Exam showed marked distress, afebrile status, BP 133/83 mmHg, HR 61 bpm, O2 saturation 97% on room air, no JVD, edema, murmurs, or chest wall tenderness, and normal lung and abdominal exams. Labs showed troponin 0.08 ng/mL, WBC 22,000/mm³ with neutrophilia and bandemia, platelets 771,000/mm³, hemoglobin 17.5 g/dL, and glucose 192 mg/dL.

case:
Newborn girl admitted to the NICU after cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery. Delivered at 40 weeks after prolonged labor and cesarean section for nonreassuring fetal status with meconium-stained amniotic fluid and breech presentation. At birth, she had limp tone and no respiratory effort; spontaneous circulation returned after 16 minutes of resuscitation with intubation, CPR, epinephrine, and saline boluses. Apgar scores were 1, 0, 0, 1, and 3 at 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20 minutes. On NICU arrival, temperature was 34.9°C, heart rate 141 bpm, blood pressure 84/59 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation 97% on mechanical ventilation. Pregnancy was complicated by maternal hepatitis C infection, treated Chlamydia trachomatis infection, gestational hypertension, and prenatal right urinary tract dilatation on ultrasound. Therapeutic hypothermia was started.

54-year-old man with polysubstance abuse and treatment-naïve hepatitis C presented with altered mental status. He was afebrile, drowsy, and hypertensive (172/110 mmHg), with jugular venous distention and bibasilar crackles. History also included a sister with renal failure of unclear cause requiring dialysis at age 45. Laboratory findings showed severe renal dysfunction (creatinine 16.0 mg/dL, BUN 99 mg/dL), mild anemia (hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL), proteinuria (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.9), rare schistocytes, elevated LDH, and low C3 with normal C4; C3 hypocomplementemia persisted during hospitalization. Urine toxicology was positive for cocaine metabolites. Kidney ultrasound showed echogenic kidneys measuring 9.8 cm and 10.3 cm.

case:
44-year-old Chinese woman with 7 weeks of progressively worsening nausea and vomiting with 13 kg weight loss. She denied abdominal pain, distension, or diarrhea. Initial treatment for presumed functional gastrointestinal disorder, including antidepressants, prokinetics, and anti-emetics, was ineffective. Eight days after admission, she developed metabolic alkalosis, acute respiratory failure, and neurological deficits. Examination showed right-sided limb paralysis, horizontal nystagmus, loss of pharyngeal reflex, decreased tendon reflexes on the right, and bilateral Babinski signs. Past history was unremarkable; gastroscopy and abdominal CT were normal. Laboratory tests showed normal liver, kidney, thyroid, autoimmune, glucose, and HbA1c results; serum AQP4-IgG was negative, but cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG was positive.
